## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the siege, the defences, the groups involved and what followed. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Khandaq for the defensive works, the name Qurayza for the group in 33:26, and the dates.
- The ayat give no casualties, no dates and no commanders; none are given in this draft.
- The sentence on sedition in 33:14 and the clause on those of the People of the Book in 33:26 are sensitive; a scholar should confirm that the wording stays within what the ayat say.
- The prophet drafts (content/stories) are separate; this event draft stays inside its own refs.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. They came from above and below  (`#they-came-from-above-and-below`)

Cited ayat: 33:9-11

> **33:9** يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَآءَتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا وَجُنُودًا لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
>
> **33:10** إِذْ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠
>
> **33:11** هُنَالِكَ ٱبْتُلِىَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُوا۟ زِلْزَالًا شَدِيدًا

### Claims

**c1** (33:9): The believers were told to remember God's favour to them when forces came against them, and God sent a wind upon them and forces they did not see; God sees what they do.

**c2** (33:10): They came upon them from above and from below; the sight swerved, hearts reached the throats, and they thought wrong thoughts about God.

**c3** (33:11): There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.

### One-minute summary

The believers were told to remember God's favour when forces came, and God sent a wind and forces they did not see [c1]. They came from above and from below, and the believers were tested and shaken [c2][c3].

### Complete story

The believers were told to remember God's favour to them when forces came against them, and God sent a wind upon them and forces they did not see; God sees what they do [c1].

They came upon them from above and from below; the sight swerved, hearts reached the throats, and they thought wrong thoughts about God [c2]. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah on the wind speaks of a favour to be remembered, and names what God sent: a wind and forces that were not seen [c1]. The next ayat describe the fear: the sight swerved and hearts reached the throats [c2].

### Kids mode

The forces came against the believers from above and below, and they were afraid and tested [c2][c3]. God sent a wind and forces they could not see [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat ask the believers to remember a favour at the very moment of fear [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat do not hide the fear or the wrong thoughts about God [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the forces were, how many, where they came from or where they stood; the ayat say from above and from below and nothing more.
- Not established: what the wind was like, how long it lasted, or what the forces they did not see were.
- Not established: how long the test lasted or how it ended in detail.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the event as a siege, the defensive works, the groups and the dates.

## 2. Fear and flight  (`#fear-and-flight`)

Cited ayat: 33:12-20

> **33:12** وَإِذْ يَقُولُ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
>
> **33:13** وَإِذْ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمْ فَٱرْجِعُوا۟ وَيَسْتَـْٔذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوْرَةٌ وَمَا هِىَ بِعَوْرَةٍ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارًا
>
> **33:14** وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُوا۟ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ لَـَٔاتَوْهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُوا۟ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرًا
>
> **33:15** وَلَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ عَٰهَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مِن قَبْلُ لَا يُوَلُّونَ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ وَكَانَ عَهْدُ ٱللَّهِ مَسْـُٔولًا
>
> **33:16** قُل لَّن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْفِرَارُ إِن فَرَرْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْمَوْتِ أَوِ ٱلْقَتْلِ وَإِذًا لَّا تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
>
> **33:17** قُلْ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَعْصِمُكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ سُوٓءًا أَوْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ رَحْمَةً وَلَا يَجِدُونَ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا
>
> **33:18** قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنكُمْ وَٱلْقَآئِلِينَ لِإِخْوَٰنِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنَا وَلَا يَأْتُونَ ٱلْبَأْسَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
>
> **33:19** أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ فَإِذَا جَآءَ ٱلْخَوْفُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أَعْيُنُهُمْ كَٱلَّذِى يُغْشَىٰ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْمَوْتِ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ ٱلْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُم بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ أَشِحَّةً عَلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ فَأَحْبَطَ ٱللَّهُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرًا
>
> **33:20** يَحْسَبُونَ ٱلْأَحْزَابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا۟ وَإِن يَأْتِ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ يَوَدُّوا۟ لَوْ أَنَّهُم بَادُونَ فِى ٱلْأَعْرَابِ يَسْـَٔلُونَ عَنْ أَنۢبَآئِكُمْ وَلَوْ كَانُوا۟ فِيكُم مَّا قَٰتَلُوٓا۟ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا

### Claims

**c1** (33:12): The hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts said that God and His Messenger had promised them nothing but delusion.

**c2** (33:13): A party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so go back; and a group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying that their houses were exposed, though they were not exposed; they only wanted to flee.

**c3** (33:14-15): Had their city been entered from its sides and they been asked for sedition, they would have given it, hesitating little; they had made a covenant with God before not to turn their backs, and the covenant with God will be asked about.

**c4** (33:16-17): They are told: flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will be enjoyed only briefly; who can protect you from God if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you? They will find no ally or helper besides God.

**c5** (33:18-19): God knows those among them who hinder others and say to their brothers: come to us; they join the fighting only a little, grudging toward you; when fear comes, they look at you as one overcome by death, and when fear goes, they scald you with sharp tongues, grudging toward good; God made their deeds fruitless.

**c6** (33:20): They think the factions have not gone; if the factions came again, they would wish to be among the desert nomads asking for news of you, and if they were among you, they would fight only a little.

### One-minute summary

The ayat tell of hypocrites who said that God and His Messenger had promised only delusion, and of a party who told the people of Yathrib to go back [c1][c2]. They say that flight will not benefit them, and that God made the deeds of those who hold back fruitless [c4][c5].

### Complete story

The hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts said that God and His Messenger had promised them nothing but delusion [c1]. A party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so go back [c2]. A group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying that their houses were exposed, though they were not exposed; they only wanted to flee [c2].

Had their city been entered from its sides and they been asked for sedition, they would have given it, hesitating little [c3]. They had made a covenant with God before not to turn their backs, and the covenant with God will be asked about [c3].

They are told: flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will be enjoyed only briefly [c4]. They will find no ally or helper besides God [c4].

God knows those among them who hinder others and say to their brothers: come to us; they join the fighting only a little, grudging toward you [c5]. When fear comes, they look at you as one overcome by death, and when fear goes, they scald you with sharp tongues, grudging toward good; God made their deeds fruitless [c5]. They think the factions have not gone; if the factions came again, they would wish to be among the desert nomads asking for news of you, and if they were among you, they would fight only a little [c6].

### Deep study

The ayat set the words of the hypocrites, their excuse of exposed houses and their earlier covenant side by side [c1][c2][c3]. They answer with a reminder that flight cannot protect from death and that no one can shield from God [c4]. The last ayat describe their conduct in fear and after fear, and give the verdict that God made their deeds fruitless [c5][c6].

### Kids mode

Some people who were not sincere said the promise was only a delusion, and tried to leave [c1][c2]. The ayat say that running away cannot save anyone from death, and that no one can shield them from God [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show how fear brings out words that were not believed in the heart [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat remind them that flight cannot protect from death [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the hypocrites and the party were by name, or how many; the ayat do not name them.
- Not established: which houses were exposed, or whether any attempt to leave was made; the ayah says only what they asked.
- Not established: what covenant they had made before; the ayah says they had pledged not to turn their backs.
- Not established: how long the fear lasted or when the factions went.

## 3. The believers' answer  (`#the-believers-answer`)

Cited ayat: 33:21-24

> **33:21** لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِى رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا
>
> **33:22** وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلْأَحْزَابَ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلَّآ إِيمَٰنًا وَتَسْلِيمًا
>
> **33:23** مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا۟ مَا عَٰهَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ فَمِنْهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُۥ وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَنتَظِرُ وَمَا بَدَّلُوا۟ تَبْدِيلًا
>
> **33:24** لِّيَجْزِىَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ وَيُعَذِّبَ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ إِن شَآءَ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا

### Claims

**c1** (33:21): There is a good example for you in the Messenger of God, for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much.

**c2** (33:22): When the believers saw the factions, they said: this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth; it only increased them in faith and submission.

**c3** (33:23): There are men among the believers who were true to what they pledged to God; some have fulfilled their vow and some are still waiting, and they have not changed at all.

**c4** (33:24): This was so that God may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in mercy; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that there is a good example in the Messenger of God, and that the believers, when they saw the factions, said that this was what God and His Messenger had promised [c1][c2]. They say that it only increased them in faith and submission, and that some were true to what they pledged [c2][c3].

### Complete story

There is a good example for you in the Messenger of God, for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much [c1].

When the believers saw the factions, they said: this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth; it only increased them in faith and submission [c2].

There are men among the believers who were true to what they pledged to God; some have fulfilled their vow and some are still waiting, and they have not changed at all [c3]. This was so that God may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in mercy [c4].

### Deep study

The same sight, the factions, is met with fear in one group of ayat and with increased faith in these [c2]. The ayat distinguish between those who have fulfilled their vow and those who still wait [c3]. They end with the purpose: to reward the truthful and to leave the hypocrites to God's will to punish them or turn to them [c4].

### Kids mode

The believers saw the factions and said that this was what God and His Messenger had promised [c2]. It only made them believe more and submit more [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show one sight meeting different hearts [c2]. Another is that the ayat praise men who were true to their pledge to God [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the men who fulfilled their vow are by name, or what the vow was; the ayah says only that they were true to what they pledged.
- Not established: what the promise they recalled was; the ayah says only that it was what God and His Messenger promised.
- Not established: who the ones waiting are, or for what.
- The ayat do not say how the example of the Messenger applies in detail.

## 4. What God did  (`#what-god-did`)

Cited ayat: 33:25-27

> **33:25** وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنَالُوا۟ خَيْرًا وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلْقِتَالَ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزًا
>
> **33:26** وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَٰهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعْبَ فَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقًا
>
> **33:27** وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيَٰرَهُمْ وَأَمْوَٰلَهُمْ وَأَرْضًا لَّمْ تَطَـُٔوهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرًا

### Claims

**c1** (33:25): God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good; and God spared the believers from fighting; God is strong and mighty.

**c2** (33:26): He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and cast terror into their hearts; some you killed and some you took captive.

**c3** (33:27): He made them inherit their land, homes and wealth, and a land they had not trodden; God has power over all things.

### One-minute summary

God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, and spared the believers from fighting [c1]. He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and the ayat say that some were killed and some taken captive [c2].

### Complete story

God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good; and God spared the believers from fighting; God is strong and mighty [c1].

He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and cast terror into their hearts; some you killed and some you took captive [c2]. He made them inherit their land, homes and wealth, and a land they had not trodden; God has power over all things [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat go from the turning back of the forces to the fate of those who had backed them, and end with what was inherited [c1][c2][c3]. The description of the People of the Book is by what they did, backing the forces, and not by name [c2].

### Kids mode

God turned back those who came against the believers, and they gained nothing [c1]. He also dealt with those who had backed them, and made the believers inherit their land [c2][c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat end the account with statements about God's strength and power [c1][c3]. Another is that the ayat describe a group by what it did, backing the forces, and then by what befell it [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the People of the Book who backed the forces were, how many were killed or taken captive, or where the strongholds were.
- Not established: what land they had not trodden, or what became of it.
- Not established: the date or the length of the events.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the group, the place and the details of the events that these ayat are linked with; no names are given in the ayat.
